newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner trade profit drop surprising - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner trade profit drop surprising - analysts.

text.p: FRANKFURT, Oct 31 - Analysts on Thursday said they were surprised at the drop in Dresdner Bank AG's trading profits in the first nine months of 1996, but said the German bank's overall earnings were in line with expectations.

Dresdner Bank reported a 29.7 percent rise in nine-month operating profits to 1.89 million marks, in the range of expectations, but its trading income dropped 14.8 percent to 456.2 million marks in the period.
"The trading result was disappointing," said Dieter Hein, analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.

"This in effect means that Dresdner barely earned 100 million marks on its own account in the last six months," Hein said, referring to Dresdner's indication earlier this year that it had earned some 400 million marks trading income in the first quarter.
Hein and other analysts said they were looking forward to a meeting with Dresdner on Monday to find out more about the trading income question.
Dresdner itself said it would make up for the weak trading income in the last quarter, when it should realise pending income.
A spokesman said the bank expects to earn 200 million marks in the fourth quarter on its own account, which would put it back within analysts' forecasted range by year-end.
Dresdner's overall earnings were in line with expectation. Analysts' forecasts for its operating earnings had ranged from 1.82 billion marks to 2.04 billion and the average was 1.95 billion marks.
The stocks reacted moderately well to the news, rising 10 pfennigs to 41.10 marks in floor dealings.
"The only real surprise was trading income and the rest was more or less in line," said Natalia Grasegger, analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank AG in Munich.
"I had forecast 1.97 billion marks operating profit but I think this will be compensated later in the year by improved interest income, which is already doing very well," Grasegger added.
Dresdner's net interest income, boosted by the integration of merchant banking unit Kleinwort Benson, rose 7.5 percent to 4.997 billion marks in the period.

Grasegger, who has a buy recommendation on Dresdner, said she saw no reason to change her earnings forecasts for the stock from her current DVFA estimate of 3.05 marks per share in 1996 and 3.35 marks in 1997.
However Hein, who is expecting Dresdner's year-end profits to rise 30 percent, said he had not yet decided whether to alter his forecasts and would await more information from Dresdner.
"There were surprises that we need to have clarified," BZW, Frankfurt's research department said.
